name: BACH_0171
markdown:
## Bottom line
The model suggests non-malignant breast tissue, most likely **Normal (77%)**, with **Benign (20%)** still possible; the probability of invasive carcinoma is **0.14%** [F1]. You can place reasonable trust in the "not invasive" part of this call because image quality is good and all agreement signals are concordant, but you need to decide Normal versus Benign yourself.

## Confidence and uncertainty
This call is confident about malignancy and ambiguous within the non-malignant categories. The calibrated probabilities put almost all the mass on Normal and Benign. In situ carcinoma gets **3%** and invasive carcinoma **0.14%**. The 90% conformal set is {Normal, Benign} [F1]. This means that, at the dataset-level 90% guarantee, the model cannot separate these two classes. It also means both malignant categories fall outside the set. The case was flagged (tier 3) only because the set has more than one class. Nothing in the evidence points to a high-risk reason for the flag.

The input itself does not look suspect. Reliability is **0.97**, the OOD percentile is 0.36 (a fairly typical image), the reliability flag is off, and all 12 regions passed QC [F6]. CONCH and MUSK agree on the top class, and all 5 of the 5 most similar reference images are labelled Normal [F5].

I don't see a need to defer this case for safety reasons. The open question is the Normal-versus-Benign distinction, and that rests with the pathologist's own review.

| Signal | Value | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| P(Normal) / P(Benign) | **77%** / **20%** | Most of the mass is on Normal, with a meaningful Benign share |
| P(InSitu) / P(Invasive) | 3% / **0.14%** | Malignancy is very unlikely according to the model |
| Conformal set (α = 0.1) | {Normal, Benign} | The model cannot separate these two at the 90% guarantee; malignant classes are excluded |
| Reliability | **0.97**, not flagged | The image looks like the training data |
| OOD percentile | 0.36 | Typical for the training distribution |
| QC regions kept | 12 of 12 | The whole image was usable |
| CONCH vs MUSK top class | Agree | Two independent models give the same top class |
| Neighbor agreement | 5/5 Normal | The nearest reference images share the suggested label |
| Worklist flag | Tier 3, reason: set size > 1 | Flagged for the Normal/Benign ambiguity, not for risk |

## Tissue evidence behind the call
All concept scores below are **model-derived** from image embeddings. They are not measurements.

**Concepts pushing away from invasive carcinoma:**
- **Normal lobules with two-layered epithelium** [F2] is the largest contribution (**−1.21**), strongest in regions 2, 10 and 11. Intact lobules with a luminal and myoepithelial layer would be biologically consistent with non-malignant tissue. However, this concept failed its spot check (**0/20**), so it is **unreliable**. Its high score should not be read as evidence that normal lobules are actually present.
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** [F3] contributes **−0.71**, strongest in regions 7, 8 and 11. Bland stroma without infiltrating epithelium argues against stromal invasion. This concept passed its spot check (20/20).
- **Gland/tubule formation** [F4] contributes **−0.57**, strongest in regions 1, 6 and 9. Preserved tubule formation is the opposite of the architectural loss seen in carcinoma. It passed its spot check (18/20), but it is a text-prompt-only score whose caption consistency check failed.

**Concepts pointing toward invasive carcinoma (both weak in this case):**
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (spot check 19/20) scores about typical for the image overall. Its total contribution is slightly negative (−0.10). At the regional level it is above typical in regions 8 (0.63), 11 (0.60) and 7 (0.37).
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (spot check 18/20) is above typical and strongest in regions 7 and 8. Its contribution is negligible (+0.05).
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (spot check 12/20) is below typical overall, and its top region is 0. Its contribution is small (+0.22).

**Other concepts:** Mitoses (region 6), necrosis (region 3) and lymphocytic infiltrate (region 5) contribute very little. Their spot checks are poor: **0/20** for mitoses (also flagged weak), **3/20** for necrosis and **8/20** for lymphocytes. They are **unreliable** and should not be used to support or refute anything.

**Measured cell features (HoVer-Net):** These were measured on **regions 1, 5 and 6 only**, which is 3 of 12 regions. None of these features feeds the classifier (each contribution is null), so they describe the tissue without explaining the model's decision.
- **Mean nuclear area: 46.7 µm²**, smaller than every image in the reference set (percentile 0) [F7]. Small, uniform nuclei fit non-malignant epithelium. The app's summary phrases this as "no benign reference case has a lower nuclear size," but the JSON only places it against the reference set as a whole.
- **Variability of nuclear area (CV 0.52) and nuclear shape (CV 0.14)** are both higher than in 83% of reference images. This modest variability is not by itself evidence of pleomorphism, especially with such small nuclei.
- **Cells labelled neoplastic:** density of 1,500 per mm² (86th percentile) and fraction of 0.29 (68th percentile), based on 51, 80 and 74 cells in regions 1, 5 and 6. This is a segmentation label, not a diagnosis, and it sits in regions the heatmap ranks as near-zero risk.
- **Inflammatory cells** make up 3% of nuclei, and TIL proximity is 0.81 (78th percentile). Infiltrate is mild, with some lymphocytes lying near epithelium.
- **Epithelial fraction (0.60) and dead-cell fraction (0)** are features the validation flags as pointing in the wrong direction, so I have not interpreted them.

## How far to trust these explanations
- **Region heatmap: passed the deletion test.** Removing the 3 regions it ranks as highest-risk lowers P(invasive) more than removing random regions (difference **0.011**, 95% CI 0.002 to 0.020). The test measures invasive risk, though, and does not address the Normal-versus-Benign question that is open here.
- **Concept attributions: not shown to be faithful.** In the same deletion test the concept ranking does no better than random (**0.0008**, CI −0.009 to 0.006). The single largest concept in this case, normal lobules [F2], scored **0/20** on its spot check. Mitoses scored 0/20, necrosis 3/20 and lymphocytes 8/20. These spot checks were done by an AI reviewer, not a pathologist.
- **Calibration and conformal coverage are acceptable but imprecise.** Calibration error after calibration (ECE) is **0.055**, but the CI reaches up to 0.22. Conformal coverage is **90%** (CI 76–98%), with a mean set size of 1.31. Both come from 132 test images from 24 patients.
- **Reliability score is moderately useful.** It ranks errors on simulated frozen sections with AUROC **0.70** (CI 0.59–0.86). Its good value here is reassuring but not decisive.
- **Cell measurements:** 15 of 21 spot checks were acceptable, and two features are known to point the wrong way.

Lean on the calibrated probabilities, the conformal set and the region heatmap. Treat every concept explanation, especially "normal lobules," as a hypothesis to check by eye.

## Where the evidence disagrees
- **Regions 7, 8 and 11 are the most important ones to check.** They are the heatmap's highest-risk regions (11: 0.249, 7: 0.053, 8: 0.038; region 3 is 0.076). They also carry above-typical scores for infiltrating stroma and pleomorphism, both of which passed their spot checks. Yet they are also among the top regions for benign stroma and normal lobules, so the model's reading of them is mixed.
- **Cells were not measured in the regions that matter most.** The nuclear measurements come from regions 1, 5 and 6, which are low-risk. There are no nuclear data for regions 3, 7, 8 or 11.
- **The Normal-versus-Benign split depends on unreliable evidence.** The most similar Benign reference image (BACH_0380, similarity 0.90) differs most in lymphocytes and mitoses, and both of those concepts failed their spot checks. The biggest factor favoring Normal is the normal-lobules concept, which also failed (0/20).
- **The most plausible way this case is wrong:** a benign lesion called Normal, or less likely a focus of atypia or in situ carcinoma (3%) in regions 0, 7, 8 or 11 that the model under-weighted.

## What to check on the slide
1. **Regions 2, 10 and 11:** confirm that the lobules are truly normal, with an intact myoepithelial layer. The concept can't vouch for this. Normal lobules support Normal; a proliferative or other benign lesion shifts the case to Benign.
2. **Regions 11, 7 and 8 (and 3):** look for epithelium infiltrating stroma as single cells or cords, and for nuclear pleomorphism. Bland stroma and nuclei confirm the call; true infiltration or marked atypia overturns it.
3. **Region 0:** exclude an atypical intraductal proliferation, since this is the top region for "atypical cells confined within ducts" and in situ carcinoma has 3%. Finding one would move the case out of the conformal set.
4. **Regions 1, 6 and 9:** check that the tubules and glands have benign architecture, and assess any glandular proliferation that would favor Benign over Normal.
5. **Region 6 (and anywhere else):** count mitoses by eye if needed, because the mitosis concept is unreliable. No follow-up orders were drafted, which fits the low estimated risk.

## Limits
Sepia is a research prototype and has not been clinically validated. Its explanations describe how the model behaves and are hypotheses to verify on the slide, not proof of why it reached this call.
